correctness.rationale: The linear Dirichlet interval diffusion+unit reproduction+rate-r independent reset-to-mu intensity has a principal growth rate characterized by r∫W_{q,L}(y)dmu(y)=1 with q=lambda+r-1 and W=(q-Delta_D)^-1 1. Dirichlet semigroup positivity makes the score strictly decreasing from infinity at the first pole -pi²/(4L²) to zero, hence a unique positive eigenmeasure and dominant eigenvalue; a Laplace-modulus comparison excludes higher complex spectral roots. For q>0, W(y)=[1-cosh(sqrt(q)y)/cosh(sqrt(q)L)]/q, at q=0 W=(L²-y²)/2, for q<0 W=[cos(sqrt(-q)y)/cos(sqrt(-q)L)-1]/(-q). As a function of z=y², its second derivative is strictly negative at q>0 and strictly positive at q<0 throughout the support, and zero at q=0. A strict convex-order spread of Y² at fixed mean m2 therefore shifts the root up for L<sqrt(m2+2/r) and down above, with exact common root lambda=1-r at equality. Expansion W=(L²-y²)/2-q(5L^4-6L²y²+y^4)/24+O(q²) and the implicit function theorem yield critical-width slope difference (m4_nu-m4_mu)/(24 sqrt(2+m2)) at r=1. Fresh independent high-precision evaluation of the spectral score at L=79/50, mu=±1/sqrt2 and nu=(1/2)delta0+(1/4)(delta±1), gave signs (-,+) at r=.8 and (+,-) at r=2; separate curvature finite differences checked q=±.5. Numerical cases establish only the witness; the resolvent proof is global.

value.rationale: Reset-destination dispersion is a natural, practically relevant control in lethal bounded habitats. The universal exact crossover at a second-moment-only length, a same-habitat extinction/growth reversal, and an explicit fourth-moment correction to the critical habitat width are non-obvious, reusable spectral-statistical facts extending fixed-site reset population models. They give both a structural theorem and a rigorously certified counterintuitive parameter witness.
